chapter_theme: The single song at Kariyavanagar (கரியவனகர்): a confession to courtesans who take money and turn away the penniless, a plea to be shown the feet, and praise of the battle and of Murugan who listens to songs in Tamil.

778.reading: The poet lists what the women do: show their bee-circled hair, kindle the fire of union with their eyes, spend the time in bed, give themselves to young men and ask for coins, show a peacock's grace, parade the streets, brush dust from their breasts, put face to face to rouse desire, send far away those without wealth and measure up anyone to embrace, and asks that love for them be removed, his trouble ended, and grace given by showing the feet. The praise shows the battlefield of blood, ghosts and vultures and the vel that killed the night-roamers, Murugan on the peacock with a golden garland, son of Parvati, worshipped by Valli, who in grace hears songs in Tamil at Kariyavanagar.
778.nuance: காசு கேட்கவும் and இருநிதி இலரைத் தூர நீக்கவும் (sending away those without wealth) make these courtesans. The confession is built as a string of infinitives (-வும்), each a habit of the women. கருணைய தமிழிற் பாடல் கேட்டருள் may point to the poet's own songs.
